text: "In Your light we see light." To find your lost keys in a dark room, you don't need a torch aimed at the keys. You switch on the light.
explanation:
"How precious is Your lovingkindness [chesed], O God! Therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of Your wings. They are abundantly satisfied with the fullness of Your house, and You give them drink from the river of Your pleasures" (the Hebrew is Eden, in the plural). "For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light."

You don't always need a sermon on your exact problem. When Jesus is unveiled from the Word, light floods everything, and in that light you suddenly see what to do about your marriage, your child or your business. "The entrance of Your words gives light."

text: The golden lampstand wasn't assembled from parts. It was hammered out of one talent of pure gold.
explanation:
Other tabernacle items were woven or skilfully crafted. The menorah was "beaten work": one solid piece of pure gold, hammered until its branches came out of its central shaft. It speaks of Jesus, the light inside the sanctuary for His people.

Isaiah says His "visage was marred more than any man." He was beaten beyond recognition. And just as the branches came out of the hammered shaft, the church came out of His wounded side. Jesus is the only time beauty itself became disfigured, so He could give you "beauty for ashes."

text: "Is a lamp brought to be put under a bushel or under a bed?" The bushel is commercialism; the bed is laziness. Both hide the light.
explanation:
Right after the parable of the sower, Jesus asked whether anyone lights a lamp only to cover it with a bushel measure or shove it under a bed. A bushel was a trader's measure; a bed speaks of ease and pleasure. When God gives you light, don't bury it under a life that's only about making money, or one that's only about comfort.

You have an assignment from God, often hinted at by what you love and are gifted to do. "Be always abounding in the work of the Lord": not just work for Him, but the work He gives you. And "take heed what you hear."

text: The rebuilding of the temple stalled for years. Behind the scenes, the high priest stood in filthy garments with Satan accusing him.
explanation:
When the exiles returned from Babylon, their enemies wrote to the king and the temple work stopped. It looked like politics. But Zechariah was shown what was really happening: Joshua the high priest standing before the Angel of the Lord in filthy clothes, and Satan at his right hand to oppose him.

The Lord rebuked Satan and said, "Take away the filthy garments from him… I will clothe you with rich robes." A clean turban was set on his head. Often what stalls God's work in your life isn't the obstacle outside, but condemnation inside. Let Him clothe you in His righteousness.

text: "Who are you, O great mountain? You shall become a plain." Shout "Grace, grace" to it.
explanation:
Zerubbabel, the governor, had lost heart. God's word to him was: "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit." No army or wealth required. Then: "Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain! And he shall bring forth the capstone with shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'" God even said, "His hands shall also finish it," while the building was still unfinished.

Whatever mountain looms in front of you (sickness, debt, a wayward child), speak grace to it: God's unearned, undeserved favour. When you don't even know how to pray, "Grace, grace" is a prayer.

text: "They prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah." Be careful what you listen to; you'll prosper through what you hear.
explanation:
After years of stalled building, God raised up two young prophets. Haggai stirred the people to build God's house; Zechariah encouraged the leaders with visions of grace. "So the elders of the Jews built, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah."

The word you keep hearing shapes your life. Jesus said, "Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you." The attacks come daily, so feed on the Word daily: Christ-centred, grace-filled preaching that builds you up.

text: "Before the lamp of God went out," God called young Samuel, son of Hannah, whose name means grace. God never lets His light go out.
explanation:
Eli the priest was old, his eyes growing dim, and he had let his sons corrupt the worship of God. The word of the Lord was rare. But "before the lamp of God went out in the tabernacle," while Samuel was lying down near the ark, the Lord called him by name.

Samuel was born because his mother Hannah, "grace," dared to ask God for something big. Where the church seems dim, God is raising a new generation that knows grace and dares to ask. He has never let His lamp go out, and He won't now.
